4. Two precise limitations of attempted constructions

4.1 Every lower matching coefficient can agree while the permanent changes

For even $n\ge4$, let $P_n$ be the cyclic permutation matrix, and set

$$A_n=I_n+P_n,
\qquad
B_n=(I_{n/2}+P_{n/2})\oplus(I_{n/2}+P_{n/2}).$$

Their bipartite graphs are respectively one cycle $C_{2n}$ and two disjoint cycles $C_n$. Consequently,

$$\operatorname{per}(A_n)=2,
\qquad
\operatorname{per}(B_n)=4.$$

Write

$$Z_A(z)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}m_k(A)z^k.$$

There is an exact identity

$$\boxed{Z_{B_n}(z)=Z_{A_n}(z)+2z^n.}$$

In particular,

$$\boxed{
m_k(A_n)=m_k(B_n)\quad\text{for every }0\le k<n.
}$$

Here is a short proof. The cycle partition function is

$$Z_{C_\ell}(z)=\lambda_+^\ell+\lambda_-^\ell,
\qquad
\lambda_\pm=\frac{1\pm\sqrt{1+4z}}2,$$

obtained from the transfer matrix

$$\begin{pmatrix}1&z\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.$$

Since $\lambda_+\lambda_-=-z$ and $n$ is even,

$$(\lambda_+^n+\lambda_-^n)^2
=
\lambda_+^{2n}+\lambda_-^{2n}+2z^n.$$

This proves the identity.

Thus even the entire subtop coefficient record, including the near-perfect count, does not determine the permanent.

There is also an exact conditioning formula. Put

$$s(z)=\operatorname{arsinh}\!\frac1{2\sqrt z}.$$

Then

$$Z_{A_n}(z)=2z^n\cosh(2ns(z)),$$

and

$$\boxed{
\frac{Z_{B_n}(z)-Z_{A_n}(z)}{Z_{A_n}(z)}
=\operatorname{sech}(2ns(z)).
}$$

at every $0<z\le\Lambda$.

$$[Z_{A_n}(z),Z_{B_n}(z)]$$

is valid for both inputs at every such query. This remains possible through adaptive queries. Yet no permanent interval containing both $2$ and $4$ can have ratio less than two.

They satisfy

$$\operatorname{per}(A_n)=2,
\qquad
\operatorname{per}(B_n)=4.$$

Write

$$Z_A(z)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}m_k(A)z^k,$$

where $m_k(A)$ is the number of size-$k$ matchings in the corresponding bipartite graph. Then the stronger identity

$$\boxed{Z_{B_n}(z)=Z_{A_n}(z)+2z^n}$$

holds exactly.

Consequently,

$$\boxed{m_k(A_n)=m_k(B_n)\quad\text{for every }0\le k<n.}$$

This includes the entire collection of subtop matching coefficients, not merely a fixed-order Taylor expansion. In particular, both near-perfect counts are exactly

$$m_{n-1}(A_n)=m_{n-1}(B_n)=n^2.$$

Proof

For a cycle of length $L$, its matching partition function is

$$Z_{C_L}(z)=\lambda_+^L+\lambda_-^L,
\qquad
\lambda_\pm=\frac{1\pm\sqrt{1+4z}}2.$$

This follows from the two-state transfer matrix

$$\begin{pmatrix}1&z\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.$$

Because $\lambda_+\lambda_-=-z$ and $n$ is even,

$$\begin{aligned}
Z_{B_n}(z)
&=(\lambda_+^n+\lambda_-^n)^2\\
&=\lambda_+^{2n}+\lambda_-^{2n}+2(\lambda_+\lambda_-)^n\\
&=Z_{A_n}(z)+2z^n.
\end{aligned}$$

The same construction remains doubly stochastic after replacing both matrices by half their values. This simply replaces $z$ by $z/2$, and the permanent ratio remains exactly two.
